delete.description:
The delete succeeds only while the branch still points at expectedSHA. Read the problem type, not only the status.

- 404 `https://entire.com/errors/git-write/branch-not-found`: the branch is absent on this placement.
- 412 `https://entire.com/errors/merge-preview/expected-sha-mismatch`: the branch is not at expectedSHA.
- 403 `https://entire.com/errors/git-write/branch-protected`: branch protection refuses the delete. Protection is checked before the default-branch rule, so a protected default branch also answers this.
- 409 `https://entire.com/errors/git-write/default-branch`: HEAD points at the branch.
- 403 with no type: the token does not permit the delete, or the name is in a reserved namespace.
- 404 with no type: the token cannot read the repository, or this node does not serve the route. It never means that the branch is gone.
- 400: the branch name is not a valid branch, the ref is symbolic, or expectedSHA is the zero hash or does not match the repository's hash format.
- 422: a parameter fails validation, such as a missing or malformed expectedSHA.
- 503: a dependency could not answer, such as the protection check, authorization, or a re-read after a lost race. Retry.
- Types under `https://entire.com/errors/mirror/` are the mirror problems that every write shares. A read-only placement answers 403 `https://entire.com/errors/mirror/read-only-placement`.

On a GitHub mirror, GitHub owns the ordinary branches. A ref in the Entire-owned namespace (refs/heads/entire/native/*) belongs to its owning placement. When this placement does not own the ref, the delete goes to the owner. The 404 and 412 answers then reflect this placement's view, which can lag the owner. A caller that acts on a mirror must not treat that 404 as final. Every refusal at the owner answers 409 `https://entire.com/errors/mirror/upstream-refused`. That includes a branch that is already deleted, that moved, or that is protected at the owner. An unreachable owner answers 502.

get.description:
The response lists commits newest first by committer date, not by author date. The order is deterministic: the same request over the same history returns the same sequence. Each page continues that sequence. In rare histories with clock skew, a later page can repeat a commit from an earlier page. Skip a commit SHA that an earlier page returned. The order is not topological. Under clock skew across a merge, a commit can appear before one of its children.

Read the problem type, not only the status.

- 404 `https://entire.com/errors/git-read/ref-not-found`: a requested ref does not resolve on this placement. A new repository answers this until its first push.
- 404 `https://entire.com/errors/git-read/object-missing`: an object is absent on this placement. Retry.
- 404 `https://entire.com/errors/git-read/repo-gone`: the repository has no refs and the object is absent.
- 404 with no type: the token cannot read the repository, or the cause is none of the above.

On a GitHub mirror or a ref forwarded to its owner, a 404 reflects this placement's view, which can lag the owner. A caller that acts on a mirror must not treat that 404 as final.

get.summary: Metrics per merged trail
get.description:
One item per merged trail of the project that has a TCO record,
newest merge first: ordered by merged_at descending, then repo_id,
trail number and installation. Pages hold per_page items (default 50,
maximum 200); next_cursor is present only when another page exists.
Project-wide reads include only repositories the caller can pull;
authorization filters rows before pagination. No pullable repositories
returns an empty page. Repositories restored from a cursor's filter
or sort key are reauthorized on every page; a denied repository gets
403, including when permission was revoked between pages.

A parameter given twice, or a bracketed name other than repo_id[eq],
is invalid_request. Other parameters this document does not list are
ignored. The cursor does not carry per_page, so send it with each page.
A project_id that is not a ULID gets the same 403 as a project the
caller cannot view. Methods other than GET answer 405
method_not_allowed.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: The project's ID (a ULID). Without repo_id, the caller needs view access to it and results are limited to repos the caller can pull. With repo_id, the caller needs pull access to that repo, and either view access to the project or list access to the repo with the repo installed in the project.

parameters.name: repo_id
parameters.description: Only this repo's trails, by its public ID (repo_<ULID>, as each item's repo_id). Same as repo_id[eq]; must not be empty. If both are given they must be equal. A caller admitted by repo access sends it with every page.

parameters.name: repo_id[eq]
parameters.description: Only this repo's trails, by its public ID (repo_<ULID>); must not be empty.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only trails merged at or after this RFC 3339 timestamp. Percent-encode a + in an offset (%2B), or use Z.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Only trails merged before this RFC 3339 timestamp. Percent-encode a + in an offset (%2B), or use Z.

parameters.name: has_agent_data
parameters.description: Only trails whose latest TCO version has at least one model record or phase record, including records with zero tokens. Omitted or false leaves results unchanged. Repeat has_agent_data=true with each page of a filtered list; omitting or changing it with a filtered cursor is invalid_cursor. Filtering applies before pagination.

parameters.name: has_activity
parameters.description: Only trails with agent data (at least one model record or phase record on the latest TCO version, including records with zero tokens) or runner spend (at least one runner run counted in review; a trail whose review spend is recorded but no runner ran does not qualify). Omitted or false leaves results unchanged. Repeat has_activity=true with each page of a filtered list; omitting or changing it with a filtered cursor is invalid_cursor. Combined with has_agent_data=true both apply, so only trails with agent data are returned. Filtering applies before pagination.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: A next_cursor from a previous page of the same project. It carries repo_id, since, until, has_agent_data and has_activity; repeating repo_id, since or until is allowed only with the same values. has_agent_data and has_activity must each match the cursor's value (repeat true on each filtered page; omitted means false). An empty value is invalid_cursor; omit it for the first page.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Items per page.

400.description: A parameter is invalid (invalid_request) or the cursor does not decode or disagrees with the request (invalid_cursor). A valid cursor naming a repo the caller cannot read instead gets 403.

401.description: The bearer token is not valid (unauthenticated). A request with no Authorization header is refused by the gateway before it reaches this service, and that body has no code.

403.description: The caller is not an account; or lacks view access to the project with no explicit repo_id; or a repo named explicitly or by a cursor's restored filter or sort key lacks pull access, or lacks both project view and list access with installation in the project (forbidden). The answer is the same whether or not the project or repo exists or is installed. A project-wide read with no pullable repos instead returns an empty page.

404.description: No active Agent Insights installation in the project covers the requested repo (or, without repo_id, the project has none). type is https://entire.com/errors/insights/plugin-not-installed and code is insights/plugin-not-installed; clients match type exactly. An empty trail_metrics list instead means installed with no merged trails in the window.

503.description: The token or the caller's access could not be checked, or the request ran past its 4s deadline (service_unavailable).

get.summary: Phase, development and review token totals for merged trails
get.description:
Sums all five token counters per raw phase across the project's latest
stored TCO rows from active installations. trails_with_phases counts
distinct Trails with at least one phase row, including zero-token rows.
Phase names are sorted; grouping for display stays with the client.
Uses the same merged_at window and repo scope as trail-metrics: since
is inclusive and until is exclusive. Omitted bounds are unbounded. No
pagination is needed. Project-wide totals include only repositories
the caller can pull, for both phase and review tokens. No pullable
repositories returns zero totals and an empty phases array.

development.tokens is the sum of all five counters over every phase
row in scope, review_fix included, equal to the sum of phases[] tokens;
it never counts runner tokens. review.tokens is the
sum of the four runner counters (fresh_input, output, cache_write,
cache_read) over every runner run of Trails in scope, the sum of
trail-metrics review.tokens; all runners count and none is identified. A Trail
with no runner runs adds 0, and no has_activity filter applies. A repo
covered by two active installations is counted once per installation,
as in trail-metrics and the phase totals.

Installed scopes with no rows return trails_with_phases 0, phases [],
and development and review tokens of 0. Responses permit future
additive fields; clients should ignore unknown properties and accept
new phase names. Responses from servers that predate these totals may
omit development and review; read a missing one as not available,
never as 0.
A parameter given twice, or a bracketed name other than repo_id[eq],
is invalid_request. Other undocumented parameters are ignored.
A project_id that is not a ULID gets the same 403 as a project the

get.summary: Metrics for one merged or open trail
get.description:
Returns one TrailMetrics object directly, not a page, using the same
computed data as trail-metrics, including phase tokens when available.
Only the path's project, repo and trail number are considered; query
parameters are ignored; callers cannot supply a branch.

Stored merged metrics return provisional false, unchanged. When no
stored record exists, entire-api supplies the Trail state and branch.
Open Trails return provisional true with merged_at null, computed from
ingested checkpoints at one request-time UTC cutoff. Merged Trails not
yet computed return provisional true with merged_at set to the Trail's
merge time, computed at that merged_at cutoff, the same cutoff the
stored metrics will use. Provisional Trails with no matching checkpoints
return 200 with empty models and phases arrays.
Provisional totals are not persisted and may change as work is ingested.
Successful provisional responses always include review and runner_usage.
Runner reads use the active core installation and authoritative repo/Trail ID,
enumerate all review/monitor waves, and include reported usage in every status.
Runs created at or before runner_usage.run_created_at_lte are eligible:
request-start UTC for open Trails, merged_at for provisional merged Trails.
This inclusive creation bound is NOT a frozen usage snapshot; counters are
observed as pages are fetched and may increase during enumeration.
Reads are limited to 100 pages, 10,000 raw run records (including duplicates)
and 10 seconds, respecting client cancellation. Failed usage reads,
malformed run identity/time, repeated pagination tokens and exceeded budgets
answer sanitized 503 service_unavailable, never partial-success zero.

Closed-unmerged, unknown or unreadable Trails (including upstream 403),
and merged Trails with no merged_at, answer 404 insights/not-found.
A transient Trail lookup failure or unconfigured lookup answers sanitized
503 service_unavailable, without upstream details. This is distinct from the 404
insights/plugin-not-installed for a repo with no active installation.

caller cannot view. Methods other than GET answer 405
method_not_allowed.

get.description:
Returns one TrailBreakdown object. In v1 every top-level node has kind
session and basis exact. New kinds may appear: clients render a node of
an unknown kind by its totals under a generic label and never drop it.
basis is exact or estimated. children is empty in v1; where a later
version fills it, children sum to their parent for every token field,
but not for calls.

When computed from the same ingested data, the top-level nodes sum
exactly to the same Trail's metrics totals, for calls and for every
token field. A Claude Code call repeated by resumed or forked sessions
counts once, under one session, the lowest session ID, so a resumed
session can look cheaper than it was. A session whose calls are all
counted under another session has no node, so there can be fewer nodes
than the metrics sessions count.

A merged Trail's breakdown is computed from its stored checkpoint set,
read at the record's own extractor version. A checkpoint of one of its
sessions landing later, on any branch, can change the split before the
requeued computation stores new totals: until then the response is
provisional true with merged_at set, and its sums can differ from the
stored metrics. An open Trail is provisional true with merged_at null,
computed from ingested checkpoints at one request-time UTC cutoff, and
may change as work is ingested.

Authorization and method handling are the same as for the single-trail
metrics operation. Unlike it, a merged Trail with no stored record
answers 404 insights/not-found, as do closed-unmerged, unknown or
unreadable Trails; a repo with no active installation answers 404
insights/plugin-not-installed.

get.summary: The most expensive turns of one trail for a set of phases
get.description:
Returns one TrailTurns object: the limit most expensive turns among
the trail's calls that have a share in any of the given phases,
ordered by tokens descending, then by call time, session ID and call
ID; and totals for the whole phase set, so a client can show how many
turns and tokens are not listed. A turn is one model call, identified
by session_id and call_id; turn_index is the ordinal of the human
prompt it followed (0 before the first).

The calls are the same ones the trail's metrics count: a merged
Trail's stored checkpoint set, read at the record's own extractor
version, or an open Trail's live branch at one request-time UTC
cutoff, provisional true with merged_at null, which may change as work
is ingested. A checkpoint of one of a merged Trail's sessions landing
later, on any branch, can change which calls count before the
requeued computation stores new totals: until then the response is
provisional true with merged_at set, and its totals can differ from
the stored metrics. A call split across phases counts only
its share: each token count is the call's multiplied by the summed
weight of its phases in the set. totals.tokens is the sum of the
set's per-phase totals as the metrics operation rounds them, so for
the same ingested data it equals the sum of the same Trail's phases
entries for those phases. Each listed turn is rounded on its own, so
the listed turns can differ from the totals by a few tokens when
calls are split across phases. The phase set is raw phase names;
grouping phases into activities is the client's. A phase no call has
matches nothing; a set that matches no call answers 200 with empty
turns and zero totals.

phase is required and may be repeated; limit may be given once. A
bracketed name is invalid_request; other unlisted parameters are
ignored. Authorization, method handling and the 404 cases are the
same as for the trail breakdown operation.

post.summary: Idempotently upsert a batch of fact records
post.description: The collection's only POST is the batch upsert. The body is NDJSON of entire-brain factmerge records (the module's wire contract, snake_case), identity-verified per record; one invalid record rejects the whole batch. New fact ids insert rows with server-stamped attribution from the token. Existing ids union provenance anchors and advance status one way (active to superseded or retracted, superseded to retracted); regressions are ignored, so re-uploads are idempotent and never churn the feed. Facts whose anchors match an already-merged trail are stamped with its trail id.

get.description: Pages all of a repo's facts in server-change order (updated_at ASC, fact_id ASC). No pageToken replays from the beginning; clients filter locally (e.g. by git reachability of anchor commits). A status change or trail stamp bumps a fact's position, so retractions and merges re-deliver through the feed. Unlike a finite list, any non-empty page carries a resume nextPageToken; only an empty (caught-up) page returns null.

nextPageToken.description: Resume cursor; null only when the page is empty (caught up).

Idempotent against redelivery (a repeat stamps 0). Facts uploaded later with matching anchors are stamped at upsert.

An edit whose normalized text matches an existing ACTIVE fact links to that fact instead of inserting a duplicate; matching a superseded or retracted fact is a 409 (the one-way status lattice cannot reactivate it). Normalized text that leaves the id unchanged is a no-op. Requires repo write access.

put.description: Replaces an editor document's content wholesale, for callers holding a complete document rather than a Yjs update to merge: the yjs-engine sidecar computes an in-lineage replacement from the document's current state, which is then written through the same guarded, bounded-retry loop as the merge route. Unlike a merge, a wholesale replace cannot reconcile with a concurrent write, so two orthogonal controls guard it: If-Match for concurrency, and onlyIfEmpty for "write only if there is nothing to lose" — the latter is not concurrency control and declines with a no-op rather than an error. Both are re-evaluated on every retry, so a write landing mid-flight cannot slip past a check that already passed. Rejected input and content the engine cannot apply are 422; an unreachable engine or exhausted retries are 503. Service-only, requires the sync_editor_documents platform grant. Change-description documents are read-only; writes return 403.

post.description: Merges a Yjs update into an editor document via the yjs-engine sidecar (ENT-1231): reads the current state, calls the engine, then writes the merged state and its contentJson projection conditional on the row it read being unchanged. On a conflict (another merge landed first, or the key was recreated under a new row) it re-reads and re-merges — safe because CRDT merge is commutative and idempotent — up to a bounded number of attempts, after which it 503s rather than retrying forever. 503 also covers an unreachable, slow, or misbehaving engine; 422 covers non-retryable input — a malformed account id, or an update the engine cannot apply or that exceeds its body cap. Service-only, requires the sync_editor_documents platform grant. Change-description documents are read-only; writes return 403.

post.description: Re-runs every configured native review runner against the trail's current head and also fires the trail's saved agent reviewers the way a push would, so a stuck agent reviewer recovers alongside any runner reruns. Already active same-head runs and completed reviews are preserved rather than duplicated; only newly accepted runner runs count in the response's Launched. If any runner's run is recorded failed at launch because its prompt is over the 64 KiB launch limit, the response is 422 with the message that run records, even when other runners launched. A launch refused for billing answers 422 with a message saying what to do next, and records no run. A repo whose only reviewers are saved agents answers 202 with Launched: 0; a repo with no reviewer of either kind answers 422.

post.description: Starts the requested configured trail runner against the trail's current head. Repeating a request while that runner is active returns the existing run with outcome already_in_progress; outcome already_complete means a completed review already covers this head and nothing new launched. A run recorded failed at launch because its prompt is over the 64 KiB launch limit answers 422 with the message the run records. A launch refused for billing (the free trial is used up, a monthly spend limit was reached, or billing is suspended) also answers 422, with a message saying what to do next and a code naming the reason, and records no run. A runner that only declares the push trigger (not api) is refused with 409 unless its own latest run for this trail already failed, timed out, or was canceled — this route only ever retries a real prior failure for that runner, it never grants it unconditional manual launching — and that retry is scoped to native review runners (trails_review-enabled); a merged/closed trail or one with no valid head is refused with 422, matching review-rerun's own admission.

post.description: Resolves a batch of commit shas to rows with the same shape the commits list serves, including embedded checkpoint previews with resolved session names. The map is keyed by each sha exactly as requested; the row's own commitSha is the canonical lowercase form and may differ in case from its key — join on the key, not the row field. Unknown, garbage-collected, and malformed shas are absent from the map, so callers keep whatever fallback they already hold. Diff stats come from the same git computation the commits list serves (first-parent diff); a commit whose diff missed entiredb's per-commit budget carries null stats, exactly like the list. Checkpoint preview placement follows the requested sha set — a checkpoint anchors to its latest linking commit within the set — so a commit's previews can differ from the list page's placement. Built for search-result hydration: the search index stores only index-time text, and this read overlays live row data at query time.

post.description: Re-runs every configured native review runner against the trail's current head and also fires the trail's saved agent reviewers the way a push would, so a stuck agent reviewer recovers alongside any runner reruns. Already active same-head runs and completed reviews are preserved rather than duplicated; only newly accepted runner runs count in the response's Launched. If any runner's run is recorded failed at launch because its prompt is over the 64 KiB launch limit, the response is 422 with the message that run records, even when other runners launched. A launch refused for billing answers 422 with a message saying what to do next, and records no run. A repo whose only reviewers are saved agents answers 202 with Launched: 0; a repo with no reviewer of either kind answers 422.

post.description: Claims the run for the calling service account and starts it: it is running until its result arrives or its deadline passes. A run still waiting is checked against its branch: if the branch moved past the run's commit, the run is canceled as superseded and the claim is refused as run_not_claimable; an unreadable branch is a 503. A run the account already holds, still running and before its deadline, is returned again unchanged, so a claim whose response was lost can be retried. Every call, held runs included, re-checks that the account is bound to the run's Environment, is a member of the run's repository with pull on it, and that the repository is not paused; an account that lost access never gets the prompt again. 404 run_not_found: the run is unknown or the caller may not see it. 409: run_claimed (another account holds it), run_not_claimable (it is no longer waiting) or repository_paused. The route is not scoped to a project: bindings say which Environments the account serves, and a runner talks to the cell that processes its project's repositories. Needs a service account token.

post.description: Saves a new agent in the project at version 1 and returns it with its JSON etag write token, HTTP ETag and Location. Saving runs nothing. Send preset for an Entire preset with its environment, repository_ids, triggers and is_enabled, or every field and a name for a custom agent. Send environment_id, environment (saved in the same transaction as an ordinary, reusable project record; any refusal saves nothing) or runs_on self_hosted alone (the project's managed self-hosted environment). runs_on may accompany environment_id or environment when it equals that environment's runs_on, so an agent read can be sent back; a mismatch is 422. Agent names are unique among the project's active agents, ignoring case, and a project runs each preset at most once among its active agents (409 otherwise). It selects repositories of the project and requires repository push on each, recorded as repository_added events. Saving starts no run. Idempotency-Key is required: a retry with the same key and body saves nothing and returns the agent the first attempt saved, at its current version, with Idempotency-Replayed: true; the same key with a different body returns 409. A key is scoped to the caller, the project and agents, and does not expire. Bodies use the typed request schema; unknown fields, including spec wrappers and server-owned fields, are refused. Requires canManageAgents (automation principals require project write or manage). Route requests to the project's API URL returned by Core.

Requires push on each repository it adds, and on each one it keeps when it saves a version, departed ones included. Removing a repository needs no push. context.description: Trimmed source text of the usage line (capped at 300 chars)

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor to get the next page. Absent on the last page.

number.description: The trail's number in its repo.

merged_at.description: RFC 3339, UTC for stored merged metrics; null for provisional open Trail metrics; the merge time for provisional merged-not-yet-computed Trail metrics.

models.description: Per agent and model, ordered by agent then model. Empty when the trail has no agent work.

phases.description: Tokens per phase of the trail's agent work, by raw phase name, ordered by phase. Absent when a merged trail has no phase data; always present (possibly empty) for provisional (open or merged-not-yet-computed) Trails. Not split by model.

allOf.description: Review tokens, the sum of fresh_input, output, cache_write and cache_read over the Trail's runner runs and agent runs, each distinct run counted once; all runners count and none is identified. Not included in models or phases. Summed over trail-metrics rows it equals trail-activity-summary review.tokens for the same repo and merged_at window with has_activity unset. Always present on provisional responses (consult runner_usage for availability); on stored merged metrics, present once runner spend is recorded, as tokens 0 when no runner ran. Absent means not recorded yet; read it as not available, never as 0.

notes.description: Computation caveats for provisional (open or merged-not-yet-computed) Trail metrics, including malformed transcript lines skipped, counted once per session from its latest chosen checkpoint snapshot. Absent for stored merged metrics.

ChangeSize.description: Absent when the trail has no size yet, or cannot be sized (no commit range, or EntireDB lacks one of its commits).

bucket.description: Size class over additions plus deletions; one of S, M, L, XL today.

truncated.description: True when the comparison was capped, so the counts are a lower bound.

fresh_input.description: Input tokens not served from cache.

cache_read.description: Input served from the prompt cache.

trails_with_phases.description: Distinct Trails with at least one phase row, not the number of phases or all merged Trails.

phases.description: Totals by raw phase name, sorted by name; always an array, empty when no phase rows match.

allOf.description: Development tokens, the sum of all five counters over every phase row in scope, review_fix included and runner tokens never counted; equals the sum of phases[] tokens, 0 when no phase rows match.

Review tokens, the sum of fresh_input, output, cache_write and cache_read over every runner run of Trails in scope (latest TCO row, active installation, same repo and merged_at window), all runners included. Runs are reached through each Trail's TCO row, so a merged Trail whose TCO is unavailable or not yet computed contributes nothing, as in trail-metrics. 0 when none match; runner spend not recorded yet and no runs both read as 0.

tokens.description: Token count summed over the counters named by the field that holds this object.

phase.description: Raw phase name; new names may appear.

RunnerUsage.description: Present only and always on provisional single-Trail metrics; absent on stored merged metrics. Describes recorded usage availability, not whether an open Trail can gain future runs.

status.description: Complete requires full enumeration of the Trail's runner runs and agent runs and every eligible run terminal (succeeded, failed, timeout, which includes an agent run's timed_out, or canceled) with nonempty explicit usage records. Partial also means entire-api could not list the Trail's agent runs by Change, so all of its agent runs are left out. Explicit all-zero records count as reported zero; no eligible runs is complete with review tokens 0. Partial means some eligible run is nonterminal or has absent, null or empty usageByModel, even if terminal. All reported counters remain included; partial with zero known tokens is not measured zero.

run_created_at_lte.description: UTC RFC 3339 inclusive run creation eligibility bound, not a usage-as-of snapshot. Usage counters reflect when each page was fetched.

installed.description: An active Agent Insights installation of the project covers the repo. False exactly when trail-metrics answers plugin-not-installed for this repo_id.

state.description:
The repo's processing progress, first match wins: not_installed
(installed is false); partial (some trail has agent data, model or
phase usage, and unprocessed_trails is above 0); up_to_date (some trail
has agent data and unprocessed_trails is 0); unavailable (processing
cannot make progress: trail reads are denied, another deployment
processes the repo, intake has not completed a first read within an
hour, nothing is pending and every change job failed or was
unavailable, or a checkpoint job failed); not_started (intake has not
completed a first read of the repo); backfilling (read, no agent data
yet, work pending); none_available (read, nothing pending, and no
merged trail carries agent data). New values may appear: a client that
does not know a value should show no status at all, never treat it as
healthy.

unprocessed_trails.description: Merged trails found for the repo that have no metrics at the running version and have not failed. Includes trails waiting to be reprocessed after an upgrade, which an operator's regenerate requeues.

failed_trails.description: Merged trails found for the repo that have no metrics and never will; their processing failed permanently.

last_processed_at.description: When the repo's newest trail metrics were written, RFC 3339 UTC. Rewritten by a reprocess, so it reads "last updated", not "last merged". Absent when the repo has none.

has_merged_trails.description: Intake has found at least one merged trail for the repo. A none_available repo with merged trails has no session data on them; one without has nothing merged yet.

has_open_trails.description: Whether the repo had at least one open trail when intake last read its trails. With has_merged_trails false, lets a client tell a none_available repo that its insights appear once those trails merge. Absent until intake has checked.

TokenStats.description: Token statistics are whole numbers, each null when it cannot be computed. The phase_share properties are present exactly when phase is given.

tokens_median.description: Median tokens per peer. Null when there are no peers.

tokens_p90.description: 90th percentile of tokens per peer. Null when there are no peers.

tokens_per_line_median.description: Median of each peer's tokens divided by its additions plus deletions; peers with no changed lines or a truncated comparison are left out. Null when none qualify.

trail_percentile.description: Share of peers with strictly fewer tokens than the trail given in trail

phase_share_median.description: Median, over peers, of the phase set's tokens divided by all of the peer's phase tokens (a fraction, as entire.io's activity shares; in this variant both leave out cache reads). Peers with no phase tokens, such as ones computed before phases were stored, are left out. Null when none qualify.

phase_share_p90.description: 90th percentile of the same shares. Null when none qualify.

trail_phase_share.description: The same share for the trail given in trail. Null when trail is absent

merged_at.description: RFC 3339, UTC; null for an open Trail.

notes.description: Computation caveats, as the notes of the same Trail's metrics.

nodes.description: Top-level nodes ordered by first_call_at, then id. Empty when the trail has no agent work.

kind.description: The node's kind; session in v1.

id.description: Unique among its siblings; for a session, the agent's session ID.

models.description: The node's totals split by model, ordered by model.

children.description: Child nodes, each shaped like BreakdownNode; empty in v1.

merged_at.description: RFC 3339, UTC; null for an open Trail.

notes.description: Computation caveats, as the notes of the same Trail's metrics.

turns.description: At most limit turns, highest tokens first, then by call time, session ID and call ID. Empty when no call has a share in the phase set.

session_id.description: The agent's session ID; a Claude Code call replayed by resumed or forked sessions belongs to the lowest session ID. A subagent's call has subagent:<agent_id>, the subagent's own transcript.

turn_index.description: Human prompts before this call in its session; 0 before the first.

call_id.description: The call's ID within the session

allOf.description: The call's tokens weighted by the summed weight of its phases in the set, rounded per counter.

turns.description: Every turn with a share in the phase set

allOf.description: The sum of the set's per-phase totals as the metrics operation rounds them; equals the sum of the same Trail's phases entries for the set.

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem. Branch on code, not detail.

code.description: Stable error code; clients branch on it. See https://entire.com/errors/. This service sends unauthenticated, forbidden, not_found, insights/not-found, insights/plugin-not-installed, method_not_allowed, invalid_request, invalid_cursor, internal_error and service_unavailable.

truncated.description: True when results are a bounded subset rather than exhaustive: repository enumeration was capped by the repo-access resolver (ENT-1114) or the query fan-out stopped early under the per-request memory budget (ENT-1017). Retrying does not recover the remainder while the underlying cap persists.

returned_counts.description: Per-type tally of the RETURNED (post-fold, post-cap) result list — "exact for what you can see", distinct from `counts` (corpus match counts, independent of ranking/truncation). Present only on the server-side session-fold path (ENT-1595); omitted otherwise, so a client that ignores it is unaffected.

partial.description: True when the fan-out could not query every accessible namespace (some repos errored or timed out), so results may be incomplete. Omitted when the search was complete. A missing (404) namespace — a new or never-indexed repo — does not set this.

missing_repos.description: Resolved placement ULIDs of the repos counted in `fanout.missing` (matching `accessible_repos[].repo_id`; a filter value that is a row alias echoes its home placement), so a client can tell the user which repo is still being indexed instead of showing a generic empty state (ENT-3634). Deliberately top-level, not inside `fanout`, whose values are numeric counters that clients merge by summation. Populated only when the request supplied a repo filter; omitted on unscoped searches, where hundreds of accessible repos may be unindexed. Missing repos still do not set `partial`.

accessible_repos.description: The caller's broad search scope in this cell — every repo an unfiltered search would cover, independent of any repo filter on this request (ENT-1158; parity with peregrine's accessible_repos on code search). Lets the repo-filter UI offer the authoritative searchable set instead of deriving options from filter-narrowed results. Sorted by repo full name. Omitted when empty.

repo_id.description: Storage ULID of the repo's canonical placement.

provider.description: Forge namespace the repo lives in, matching the provider stamped on result rows. Rollout: servers predating this field omit it — clients must treat an absent or empty value as "github".

matchType.description: How the result was matched. "exact" marks a known-item hit resolved by an exact/prefix identifier lookup (a pasted commit SHA) and pinned to the top, rather than ranked by relevance.

score.description: Retrieval score, normalized so higher is always better. NOT the field results are ordered by — when rerankScore is present the cross-encoder decided the order, and sorting by score undoes it. Results are already returned in rank order.

rerankScore.description: Cross-encoder relevance judgement, present only on reranked results. Where present, this is the signal the ordering was built from, and the only score comparable across repositories — bm25Score is computed per-namespace against per-repo corpus statistics.

bm25Score.description: Raw BM25 score for the keyword leg; higher is better.

annScore.description: Raw cosine distance for the semantic leg; LOWER is better. Inverted into a similarity before contributing to score.

projected.description: Marks a result synthesized from another type's document (e.g. a commit projected from a checkpoint hit) rather than a match on the type's own documents. Absent means a real match.

matchedIn.description: Session results only: which evidence matched — the session's AI/custom title (its session_title doc), its transcript (checkpoint chunks), or both. The server already orders title-matched sessions above transcript-only ones; clients render labels off this field without heuristics.

SearchTypeCounts.description: True per-type match counts from a deterministic keyword + structured-filter count pass against the index, independent of ranking, Cohere reranking, and tier truncation — NOT a tally of the returned result window. commits and prs are exact document Counts (one document per entity); checkpoints and sessions are distinct-entity counts from a bounded enumeration (see counts_lower_bound); repos is the keyword-matched repo set. repos/checkpoints/commits/prs are repo-bound, and each repo has exactly one home cell (ENT-1114 one-canonical-cell guarantee), so a gateway may sum those per-cell counts across cells. sessions are the exception: a session can be cross-linked to repos in different cells, so it is deduped within a cell but summing sessions across cells may over-count a cross-cell session (bounded, and no worse than the previous per-cell behavior).

SearchTypeCountsLowerBound.description: Per-facet flag marking whether the matching value in counts is a lower bound (true → render "N+") rather than an exact total. A facet is a lower bound when its count could not be fully accounted for: a namespace errored or timed out, the per-namespace enumeration budget was exhausted with matches remaining, or (repos) the keyword match hit its per-type cap. The zero value (false) means exact, so an absent flag defaults to exact. Composable across cells: OR the flag per facet, so any cell reporting a lower bound makes the merged facet a lower bound.

SearchTypeTruncated.description: Per-type flag marking that the returned result list for that type was capped at the per-type limit (ENT-1363): the ranked set held more results of that type than the response carries, so a tab count derived from the list is a lower bound (render "N+"). Only populated on the unfiltered (no filter_type) path, where per-type caps replace the global limit cut. The zero value (false) means complete. Composable across cells: OR the flag per type, together with any re-cap the gateway applies when merging.
